definitions.explanation: Restoring one's reputation through good results or achievements after having been criticized or disgraced. A four-character compound (yojijukugo).

examples.japanese: {今度|こんど}こそ{汚名|おめい}{返上|へんじょう}だ。
examples.english: This time, I'll redeem myself for sure.

examples.japanese: {汚名|おめい}{返上|へんじょう}を{果|は}たすために{全力|ぜんりょく}で{頑張|がんば}った。
examples.english: I gave it my all to clear my name.

examples.japanese: {前回|ぜんかい}の{大会|たいかい}で{惨敗|ざんぱい}した{選手|せんしゅ}が、{見事|みごと}に{汚名|おめい}{返上|へんじょう}を{果|は}たした。
examples.english: The athlete who suffered a crushing defeat in the last tournament brilliantly redeemed themselves.

notes:
USAGE:
A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) often used in sports and competitive contexts. Frequently paired with を{果|は}たす (to achieve/accomplish).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {汚名|おめい}{返上|へんじょう}を{果|は}たす (to successfully clear one's name)
- {汚名|おめい}{返上|へんじょう}する (to redeem oneself)
- {汚名|おめい}{返上|へんじょう}の{機会|きかい} (opportunity to redeem oneself)

WATCH OUT:
Often confused with {名誉|めいよ}{挽回|ばんかい} (recovering one's honor). Some people mistakenly say {汚名|おめい}{挽回|ばんかい}, which would literally mean "recovering one's bad name" — the opposite of the intended meaning. The correct forms are {汚名|おめい}{返上|へんじょう} and {名誉|めいよ}{挽回|ばんかい}.
